body:
label: bug
file: src/i18n/en.json

The "Malformed row" message always reported at row 1 suggests the CSV parser is miscounting columns for every row, not just the first — likely triggered by a delimiter/encoding change from the new Windows export tool (e.g. semicolon-delimited CSV or a UTF-8 BOM causing the header's first column name to be misread). Since the files look fine in a spreadsheet, this points to a parsing/row-shape validation issue rather than bad data in the uploaded file itself.

label: bug
file: src/ingest/parser.ts

The new Windows export tool almost certainly produces CRLF (`\r\n`) line endings. `parseStatement` only splits on `"\n"`, so each line (including the header) keeps a trailing `\r`. That makes the last header column come out as `description\r` instead of `description`, so `REQUIRED_COLUMNS.every(...)` fails and `assertShape` throws `errors.rowShape` for the header row itself — which is why it's always reported as "row 1" regardless of the file contents. The parser needs to strip trailing `\r` from each line (or split on `/\r?\n/`) before processing.

label: bug
file: src/ingest/parser.ts

The new Windows export tool almost certainly writes CRLF (`
`) line endings. `parseStatement` splits the input only on `"
"`, so each line (including the header) keeps a trailing `""`. That makes the last header column become `"description"` instead of `"description"`, so `assertShape`'s `REQUIRED_COLUMNS.some(column => !header.includes(column))` check fails on the very first call (`assertShape(header, header, 0)`), which is why the error always reports "row 1" regardless of the file's actual content. The fix should strip trailing `` from each line (or split on `/
|
/`) before parsing the header/fields.

label: bug
file: src/notifications/rollup.ts

The rollup scheduler ticks hourly and relies on isRollupDue()/startOfWeek() to decide, for each user, whether "now" falls within the first day of their local week at SEND_HOUR. For a timezone with a large positive UTC offset like Sydney (UTC+10/+11), the local-hour and week-start calculations appear to go out of sync with the actual local calendar day near the week boundary, so the 08:00 local-time match ends up landing on Tuesday instead of Monday. Users in timezones close to UTC (e.g. London) aren't affected, which matches the reporter's observation. The fix should be in how `isRollupDue`/`startOfWeek` derive the local day-of-week/day-boundary from `now` and `user.timezone` in this file (likely a knock-on of how `util/dates.ts` computes local day boundaries, but the scheduling logic that consumes it lives here).

label: bug
file: src/export/csv.ts

The CSV writer in `src/export/csv.ts` passes rows straight to `toDelimited` without including currency in whatever key is used to distinguish rows, so two transactions that share date, amount and description but differ only in currency end up collapsed into a single CSV line. This likely regressed when currency was added to `ReportRow` in 3.2.0 but the delimited-row construction wasn't updated to account for it.

label: bug
file: src/ingest/parser.ts

The parser splits the file on "\n" only, so files with Windows-style CRLF line endings (as produced by the new accounting export tool) leave a trailing "\r" on the last column of the header line (e.g. "description\r"). That makes `assertShape` think a required column is missing on the header row itself (index 0), which is why every upload fails immediately with "Malformed row" on row 1, even though the column structure is otherwise unchanged. The parser needs to normalize/strip "\r" when splitting lines (or split on /\r?\n/) before processing the header and rows.

label: bug
file: src/ingest/dedupe.ts

Not actually a CSV writer issue. The dedupe key used during ingestion is `[t.date, t.amount, t.description].join("|")` (src/ingest/dedupe.ts), which does not include currency. Since 3.2.0 added currency to transactions, two transactions that share date, amount and description but differ only in currency now collide on this key and the later one is dropped as a duplicate before it ever reaches csv.ts. The fix is to include `currency` in `dedupeKey`.

label: bug
file: src/notifications/rollup.ts

The rollup is scheduled by a single hourly tick (`startRollupSchedule`) that fires at the top of each UTC hour and then calls `isRollupDue`, which compares `localHour(now, user.timezone)` to `SEND_HOUR` and checks that `now` falls within the first day of the user's local week (`weekStart`).

For users whose UTC offset is ahead of UTC (e.g. Sydney, UTC+10/+11), the local-week boundary computed from `now` can land on the wrong side of the server's hourly tick grid compared to users behind or at UTC (e.g. London), so the "within the first day of week" window check silently misses the correct tick and only catches it on a later (Tuesday local) tick. That's why London users, who are closer to/behind UTC, get the email right on Monday while Sydney users get it a tick late, on Tuesday morning local time.

The scheduling/window logic in `sendWeeklyRollups`/`isRollupDue` needs to correctly account for positive UTC offsets so the due-check reliably matches the hourly tick for all time zones, not just those at or behind UTC.

label: bug
file: src/ingest/parser.ts

The parser splits the uploaded text on "\n" only, so on files with CRLF line endings (which the new Windows export tool produces) each line keeps a trailing "\r". For the header line, that means the last column name becomes "description\r", which no longer matches "description" in REQUIRED_COLUMNS, so `assertShape` reports a shape mismatch on the very first row (row 1) every time — exactly what's reported. Stripping a trailing "\r" from each line (or splitting on /\r?\n/) before parsing should fix it.

label: bug
file: src/ingest/dedupe.ts

The actual bug isn't in src/export/csv.ts — the CSV writer isn't merging rows. The culprit is the dedupe key in src/ingest/dedupe.ts, which is built from `[t.date, t.amount, t.description].join("|")` and doesn't include currency. Since 3.2.0 introduced per-transaction currency, two transactions that share date, amount and description but differ only in currency (e.g. one EUR, one USD) now collide on the same dedupe key, so one is dropped as a duplicate before it ever reaches the CSV export. The fix should add currency to `dedupeKey` (and update `keysFor`/tests accordingly).

label: bug
file: src/util/dates.ts

`startOfWeek` ignores the `tz` parameter entirely (see the `// TODO: honour tz` comment) and computes the week boundary using UTC date fields. For a user in Sydney (UTC+10/11), the UTC-based week boundary falls on a different local calendar day than for users in London, which combined with `isRollupDue`'s correct per-timezone hour check in `rollup.ts` causes the rollup to be considered "due" a day later than expected locally, so the Monday summary goes out Tuesday morning for Sydney users while London users (close to UTC) are unaffected.

label: bug
file: src/ingest/parser.ts

This looks like a CRLF line-ending issue, not a malformed file. parseStatement() splits the input only on "\n" (lines.split("\n")), so when a file uses Windows-style "\r\n" line endings (likely from the new accounting export tool), each line keeps a trailing "\r". For the header line this means the last column name ends up as e.g. "description\r" instead of "description", so REQUIRED_COLUMNS.some(...) fails to find "description" in the header and assertShape() throws errors.rowShape for row 1 (the header check runs with index 0, reported as row 1) every time, regardless of the actual column layout.

Fix should strip trailing "\r" from each line (or split on /\r?\n/) before processing the header and rows in src/ingest/parser.ts.

label: bug
file: src/util/dates.ts

The weekly rollup send time is gated by `isRollupDue`, which checks `localHour(now, user.timezone)` correctly, but also computes `startOfWeek(now, user.timezone)`. That function ignores its `tz` parameter entirely (see the `// TODO: honour tz` comment) and derives the week start using UTC day-of-week/hour. For users ahead of UTC, like Sydney (UTC+10/11), the UTC calendar date can roll over a day later than their local date, shifting when the week boundary—and therefore the Monday send—lands, so the email goes out a day late. London users are close enough to UTC that this doesn't manifest. `startOfWeek` needs to compute the week start using the user's local time zone instead of UTC.

label: bug
file: src/export/csv.ts

The CSV writer itself just writes the rows it's given via toDelimited, with no merging logic — so the deduplication/merging of rows with identical date, amount, and description (but different currency) must be happening upstream in the query/report-row generation that feeds writeCsv, which currently doesn't appear to treat currency as part of the row's identity. Since 3.2.0 added currency to transactions, the row-key logic needs to be updated to include currency so rows that differ only by currency aren't collapsed into one during export.

label: bug
file: src/ingest/parser.ts

The parser splits input only on "\n" (`text.split("\n")`) and never strips a trailing "\r". Windows tools typically emit CRLF line endings, so the last field of the header line becomes "description\r" instead of "description". That fails the `REQUIRED_COLUMNS.includes` check in `assertShape`, which throws `errors.rowShape` for the header itself (index 0 → "row 1") regardless of the actual data — matching the report that every upload now fails and always cites row 1 since finance switched to a new Windows export tool that likely writes CRLF line endings. The fix is to strip a trailing "\r" from each line (or split on /\r?\n/) before parsing.
